NvSci Memory Management Kernel Driver
=====================================

Description:
Linux kernel module for memory allocations and secure buffer sharing
Version:
1.0

Build NvSci MM KMD for DRIVE OS x86
===================================

1) install kernel header package
sudo apt-get install linux-headers-`uname -r`

check version of desktop using "uname -r" command.
kernel version must be 5.4.0-104+.

2) build
cd nvsci_mm
make -C /lib/modules/`uname -r`/build M=${PWD} modules

3) module parameters:
  a) max_pending_exports: the maximum number of simultaneous/active exports by single client. Default value: UINT_MAX
  b) [gid_start:gid_end]: the range of Linux Group ID which will have access to device node. Default value: [0:0] i.e. only accessible to root.
  c) enable_debug: enable debug logs. Set this to any value greater than 0 to enable the logs. Default value: 0

4) install NvSci MM KMD
  a) with default parameter: sudo insmod nvsci_mm.ko
  b) with custom parameters: sudo insmod nvsci_mm.ko max_pending_exports=4096 gid_start=1000 gid_end=2000 enable_debug=1
  NOTE: Make sure to remove stale "/dev/nvsci_mm" device nodes before installing the kernel module.

5) remove NvSci MM KMD
sudo rmmod nvsci_mm

6) clean
make -C /lib/modules/`uname -r`/build M=${PWD} clean

NOTES
=====
nvsci_mm.c leverages implementation from system_heap.c.
A copy of system_heap.c is maintained here for reference.

NvSciIpc kernel driver
======================

Description:
Linux kernel module for secure buffer sharing
Version:
1.0

Build NvSciIpc KMD for DRIVE OS x86
===================================

1) install kernel header package
sudo apt-get install linux-headers-`uname -r`

check version of desktop using "uname -r" command.
kernel version must be 5.4.0-104+.

2) build
cd nvsciipc
make -C /lib/modules/`uname -r`/build M=${PWD} modules

3) install NvSciIpc KMD
sudo make -C /lib/modules/`uname -r`/build M=${PWD} modules_install
sudo depmod -a

nvsciipc.ko will be installed in /lib/modules/`uname -r`/extra/nvsciipc.ko

[NOTE] If kernel module installation is failed by missing signing key, follow steps below

** create x509.genkey
echo -e "[ req ] \n\
default_bits = 4096 \n\
distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name \n\
prompt = no \n\
x509_extensions = myexts \n\
\n\
[ req_distinguished_name ] \n\
CN = Modules \n\
\n\
[ myexts ] \n\
basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE \n\
keyUsage=digitalSignature \n\
subjectKeyIdentifier=hash \n\
authorityKeyIdentifier=keyid" > x509.genkey

** generate signing key
openssl req -new -nodes -utf8 -sha512 -days 36500 -batch -x509 -config x509.genkey -outform DER -out signing_key.x509 -keyout signing_key.pem

** move signing key to kernel module folder of desktop
sudo mv signing_key.* /lib/modules/`uname -r`/build/certs/

4) clean
make -C /lib/modules/`uname -r`/build M=${PWD} clean

5) load NvSciIpc KMD
You can load NvSciIpc KMD during desktop boot.
sudo vi /etc/modules-load.d/modules.conf
add "nvsciipc" to this file

For manual loading KMD, do "sudo insmod nvsciipc.ko"

This repo contains the following kernel modules:
- Name: NvSci Memory Management Kernel Driver
  Version: 1.0
  Description: Linux kernel module for memory allocations and secure buffer sharing

- Name: NvSciIpc kernel driver
  Version: 1.0
  Description: Linux kernel module for secure buffer sharing

nvsci_mm v1.0 and nvsciipc v1.0 are part NVIDIA DRIVE OS 6.0.8.0 release.
